The graph above has neither, so 6*7 is answered with {"question": "6*7", "answer": "42"}.
Orchestration: how a main agent hands off to its team. Events and streaming: the events a remote turn produces.

A skill is a set of instructions for one kind of task — how to write a release note, how to review a contract, the steps of a deployment — kept in a Markdown file. The agent always sees a one-line index of its skills, and reads a skill in full only when the task calls for it. Dozens of skills cost the context a few hundred tokens until one is needed. Use a skill for know-how that applies to some tasks and not others. Instructions that apply to every message belong in the agent's instruction, or in standing instructions. Skill files use the agentskills.io format, so skills written for other tools that use it work here, and the other way round.

A skill is a SKILL.md file: YAML frontmatter, then the instructions in Markdown. --- name: user-journeys description: How to write a user journey document. Use when asked to draft or review one. --- Write user journeys from the user's point of view. ## Structure 1. Persona 2. Goal 3. Steps ## Review checklist - Every step has an observable outcome. Key Description name The skill's name. Defaults to the name of the directory holding SKILL.md, or to the file name without .md. description What the skill is for and when to use it. The model chooses a skill from this line alone, so write it for that. Without one, the first line of the body is used, which is rarely written for the purpose. version Free-form, for your own tracking. enforcement advisory (default) or required. See Required skills. metadata.requires What the skill needs to be usable. See Requirements. Each ## heading starts a section. The model can read one section of a skill instead of the whole file, which keeps a long skill cheap. A directory of skills can hold both layouts side by side, and group them in folders: skills/ ├── user-journeys/ │ └── SKILL.md # a skill with its own directory, for supporting files ├── release-notes.md # a single-file skill └── writing/ # a group: every skill under it is read └── essays/ └── SKILL.md A directory holding a SKILL.md is one skill, and nothing inside it is read as another. Any other directory is a group, entered at any depth. A single-file skill is only read directly in the listed directory. Hidden folders and dependency folders such as node_modules or venv are skipped, and no symbolic link is followed, including the listed directory itself.

A skill can declare what it needs, under metadata.requires or as top-level keys: --- name: release-notes description: How to write release notes. Use when preparing a release. metadata: requires: bins: [git] env: [GITHUB_TOKEN] os: [darwin, linux] tools: [read_file] external_files: - scripts/ - ../shared_helper.py --- Key Met when bins Each program is on the PATH. env Each environment variable is set and not empty. os The platform is one of those listed, as Python's sys.platform names it: darwin, linux, win32. tools The agent has each of these tools. external_files Each file the skill needs besides its SKILL.md exists. external_files lists paths relative to the SKILL.md, with forward slashes; .. is allowed, an absolute path is not. An entry can be a file, or a folder, meaning every file under it. Nothing is copied: the files must already be where the skill says. A skill whose requirements are not met stays in the index, marked with the reason, for example [unavailable: env 'GITHUB_TOKEN'] or [unavailable: file 'scripts/' (does not exist)], so the model knows it exists and why it cannot use it. Requirements are checked on every turn, so a missing file put back counts from the next message.

An agent reads its skills through a SkillsRuntime: from domyn.agents import Agent from domyn.agents.skills import LocalDirSkillSource, SkillsRuntime agent = Agent( name="Writer", description="Writes product documents", instruction="Help the user write product documents.", llm_provider=llm, skills=SkillsRuntime(source=LocalDirSkillSource(paths=["./skills"])), ) LocalDirSkillSource reads every skill in paths. When two directories hold a skill of the same name, the one in the earlier directory is used. A relative path is resolved against the current directory, and ~ is expanded. Skills can also be given as text, with no files: from domyn.agents.skills import InMemorySkillSource SkillsRuntime(source=InMemorySkillSource(skills={ "tone": "---
description: House tone of voice. Use for any customer-facing text.
---
Be warm and brief.", })) In a YAML configuration, skills is declared on the agent: agents: - name: Writer ... skills: source: type: local_dir paths: [./skills] Skill files are read again on every turn, so an edited skill applies from the next message. In a team, each agent has its own skills.

On every model call of a turn, the agent's skills are added to the request as a message right after the system prompt. By default it is the index: Available skills (call skill_view to read one in full): - release-notes: How to write release notes. Use when preparing a release. - user-journeys: How to write a user journey document. Use when asked to draft or review one. The agent also gets a skill_view tool, added automatically. When a skill looks relevant, the model calls skill_view(name="user-journeys") for the whole skill, or skill_view(name="user-journeys", section="Review checklist") for one section, and reads it as the tool's result. The result starts with the skill's file: Skill: user-journeys [file: skills/user-journeys/SKILL.md] — a real file you can read and edit with your file tools when asked to change this skill. ... The path is there so that an agent asked to change a skill knows where it is, and so that a skill can name its own files relative to it. A skill added in full before the turn (see Choosing skills before the turn) starts the same way. Whether the agent can open the file depends on its tools.
documents.s: How a skill reaches the model

documents.t: The index has a budget, max_index_chars. When the skills do not fit, none is left out: all of them are shown in a shorter form, the first that fits of every description whole; every description cut to max_description_chars; names only, on one line: Also available, by name only: release-notes, user-journeys, .... The same form is used for every skill, so which skill keeps its description never depends on its name. A required skill is always shown whole. If even the names do not fit, the index lists the names that do and ends with how many it left out, so the model knows there are more and can find them with skill_search.
documents.s: When the index does not fit

documents.t: The agent also gets a skill_search tool. It searches every skill, including those the index shows by name only or not at all, and answers with the best matches, at most 10, each with its description cut to 120 characters. It never lists the whole catalogue: query is required, and limit (default 5) is capped at 10. The search is done by a model, given the query and the catalogue: skills and queries may be in different languages, and a model matches them by meaning. That model is the agent's own unless search.provider names another. If it fails, does not answer within search.timeout_s, or there is none, the search falls back to matching words, ignoring accents and comparing parts of words, so that close languages still meet; the result then says so. In domyn run, the status line at the start of a session says when the index is over its budget, and /skills says in which form the model sees the skills.

The selector decides whether some skills are read in full before the model starts, instead of on request: type Class What the model gets index IndexSelector Default. The index only. The model reads skills with skill_view. all AllSkillsSelector The index, followed by the full text of every usable skill. Costs context for every skill, used or not. llm LLMSelector Each time the agent starts working on a task, before its first model call, a separate model call is given the index and the task and picks the skills it needs. Those are added in full, or the one section that applies. If that call fails, times out or picks nothing, the turn goes on with the index only. from domyn.agents.skills import LLMSelector SkillsRuntime(source=LocalDirSkillSource(paths=["./skills"]), selector=LLMSelector(max_expansions=2)) skills: source: {type: local_dir, paths: [./skills]} selector: {type: llm, max_expansions: 2} With every selector, the whole index stays in the request, so the model can still open a skill the selector did not pick.

SkillsRuntime: Option Type Default Description source LocalDirSkillSource | InMemorySkillSource required Where the skills come from. In YAML: type: local_dir with paths, or type: memory with skills. selector selector IndexSelector See Choosing skills before the turn. index_sections bool False Lists each skill's sections in the index. Useful when the model should ask for one section without opening the skill first; costs context on every request. budget SkillBudget see below Limits on how much skill text enters the request. search SkillSearch see below How skill_search searches. SkillBudget: Option Type Default Description max_index_chars int 10000 Size of the index. Over it, skills are shown in a shorter form: see When the index does not fit. max_description_chars int 120 Length a description is cut to when the index does not fit with whole ones. max_body_chars int 20000 Total size of the skills added in full before the turn. max_expansions_per_turn int 5 How many skills can be added in full before the turn. SkillSearch, under search: Option Type Default Description provider str the agent's provider Name of a registered provider to search with, as for LLMSelector. timeout_s float 10.0 Seconds to wait for the model before matching words instead. generation_params dict {} Passed to the provider with the request. With a reasoning model, turn its thinking off here, as the provider spells it: for Qwen3 served by vLLM, {chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: false}}. max_candidates int 1000 Past this many skills, the model is shown only the best word matches. description_chars int 120 Length descriptions are cut to, in what the model searches and in the results. instruction str built in Replaces the prompt of the search call. {limit} is replaced with the number of results asked for. skills: source: {type: local_dir, paths: [./skills]} search: {provider: small_model, timeout_s: 5} LLMSelector: Option Type Default Description provider str the agent's provider Name of a provider registered with @llm_provider, to pick skills with a smaller, faster model. A provider declared under llm_providers in a YAML file is not registered, so it cannot be named here. An unknown name falls back to the agent's provider, with a warning in the log. max_expansions int 3 How many skills, or sections, it may pick. timeout_s float 10.0 Seconds to wait for the pick before going on with the index only. instruction str built in Replaces the prompt of the picking call. {limit} is replaced with max_expansions.

A skill with enforcement: required is a rule the agent must not run without, such as a compliance policy. If its requirements are not met, the turn is refused before the agent does anything: the stream is agent_start followed by error_occurred, with error_code RequiredSkillUnavailable and a message naming the skill and what is missing: Cannot run this turn: required skill(s) unavailable for agent 'Advisor': compliance (unavailable: env 'COMPLIANCE_RULES_URL') The check covers every agent of the team, including those the turn would not have reached. Fixing the requirement is enough: the next message runs normally. An advisory skill that is not usable never blocks a turn: it is marked in the index, and no selector adds it in full.

The interactive CLI loads a skill only because its configuration names it: the paths of the agent's skills source, in ~/.domyn/config.yaml or in the file passed to domyn run. Nothing else is searched, and there is no option that adds a directory. When two skills share a name, the one listed earlier wins. domyn setup fills that list. It asks about three kinds of skill, built-in ones first, and writes them in this order: The project's own skills. One yes/no question: load skills from ./.domyn/skills and ./.agents/skills in the folder domyn run starts in. Yes writes both paths as they are, relative, so they are read again on every turn from whichever folder the session starts in, and a skill added to either is loaded from the next message. When both hold a skill of the same name, ./.domyn/skills wins. It puts the text of a repository you cloned into the prompt, which is why it is a question. A folder of your own skills. The wizard reads the folder once and lists each skill in it by its absolute path. Nothing is copied: each skill is read from where it is. A skill added to that folder later is loaded only after you run domyn setup again and give the folder again. The built-in skills. A checklist, by group. The ones you tick are copied into ~/.domyn/builtin-skills and listed by absolute path. Every domyn setup deletes and rewrites ~/.domyn/builtin-skills, so an edit made there is lost and nothing of yours belongs there; to change a built-in skill, untick it and keep your own copy in ./.domyn/skills. The skills inside the package are not a fallback: a configuration that lists none has none. So a project skill wins over a skill of yours, and both win over a built-in of the same name. A relative path is read from the folder domyn run starts in. When a listed path goes through a symbolic link, or is not there, domyn run says so when it starts, except that a missing ./.domyn/skills or ./.agents/skills is not reported, because most folders have neither. It also names any listed skill whose external_files are missing. --expand-skills reads every skill in full up front (the all selector), and --skill-sections lists sections in the index. The skill directories are also reachable by the session's file tools, so you can ask the agent to edit a skill; writing still asks for your approval. Inside a session, /skills lists the skills with their files and sections, and /skill <name> shows one in full. From the shell: Command What it does domyn skills Lists the skills the configuration loads, with their files, and why any is unavailable. domyn skill show <name> Prints one skill the global ~/.domyn/config.yaml loads, with its file and sections. <name>#<section> prints one ## section. domyn skill remove <name> Removes the entry that names the skill, its folder or its .md file, from ~/.domyn/config.yaml. The files stay where they are. A skill loaded through a listed folder, such as ./.domyn/skills, has no entry of its own, so nothing is removed and the command says how to stop loading it. --project, for a project's own ./.domyn/config.yaml, is not supported.
Standing instructions: instructions that apply to every message. YAML configuration: declaring skills in a YAML file. Sessions and commands: skills in a terminal session.

Standing instructions are markdown files whose text is added to an agent's system prompt on every turn. They let you change how an agent behaves without editing its definition: your tone and preferences in one file, the project you are working on in another. File What it says Follows SOUL.md Who the agent is for you: tone, language, standing preferences, things it must not do You, in every project AGENTS.md What the agent is working on: the project, its conventions, where things are The task, so it changes when the task does Any other file A one-off brief, such as today's task One session AGENT.md is accepted in place of AGENTS.md; when a directory has both, AGENTS.md is read.

The interactive CLI reads the standing instructions its configuration declares, and nothing else: there is no command-line option for them, and ~/.domyn is not read. domyn setup asks two questions, after the agent's name and before the agent's own instruction: A folder or file with your SOUL.md / AGENTS.md. A file is saved as you give it. A folder is searched once, subfolders included: its first SOUL.md and every AGENTS.md are saved, each by its absolute path. An edit to one of those files reaches the next message, but a file added to the folder later is read only after you run domyn setup again. Unlike the other questions, an empty answer removes the current paths, so the wizard prints them first. Whether to load SOUL.md / AGENTS.md from ./.domyn and ./.agents in the folder domyn run starts in. Yes writes both paths as they are, relative, so they are read again on every turn from whichever folder the session starts in, subfolders included, and a file added there is read from the next message. domyn's own folders under .domyn, such as conversations and skills, are not searched. This puts the text of a repository you cloned into the system prompt on every turn, which is why it is a question. The paths are written in that order, so your own SOUL.md wins over a project's, and a project's AGENTS.md comes after yours. To change them, run domyn setup again or edit standing_instructions in ~/.domyn/config.yaml. No symbolic link is followed: not a listed path, not a folder on the way to a relative one, and not a file in a listed folder. A cloned repository could otherwise link its AGENTS.md to any file on your machine and have it sent to the model. The line printed when the session starts names the files in use, and says so again when one is added or removed. /config shows the paths your configuration declares. They apply to the main agent only.

On every turn, the files are read again and their text is placed in the system prompt, right after the agent's own instruction, which is never replaced. Each file is a block headed by its name and absolute path: You are a coding assistant. [SOUL.md — /home/me/notes/SOUL.md] Answer in British English. Be terse. [AGENTS.md — /home/me/work/billing/AGENTS.md] You are working on the billing service. [brief.md — /home/me/work/billing/brief.md] Today: fix the invoice rounding bug. One soul. An agent has one identity, so only the first SOUL.md in the order of the paths is used; any later one is not read. An empty SOUL.md counts as none, and the next one takes its place. Order. The SOUL.md comes first, then every AGENTS.md, then the other files, whatever the order the paths were given in. Within one kind, the order of the paths is kept. When two instructions conflict, models tend to follow the later one, which is why the most specific should come last. Every turn. An edit to a file reaches the next message, without restarting the session. A file that is missing or empty adds nothing, and a file that cannot be read is skipped with a warning. The path in the header tells the agent which file a rule comes from, so you can ask it why it does something and learn which file to edit. Each file once, even when it is reached through two paths.

The text of all standing instructions together, not counting the headers, is limited to 32 KiB (max_bytes), because they are sent with every request and no compaction can shorten them. Over the limit, the file that crosses it is cut at the limit, and its header says (truncated: instruction budget exceeded). The files after it, in the order above, are left out. Both are logged as a warning.

Any agent can declare its own standing instructions, in YAML or in Python. An agent that declares none has none: a team member does not inherit them from the main agent. agents: - name: Assistant ... standing_instructions: source: type: local_dir paths: [./instructions, ~/notes/brief.md] from domyn.agents.instructions import InstructionRuntime, LocalDirInstructionsSource agent = Agent( ..., standing_instructions=InstructionRuntime( source=LocalDirInstructionsSource(paths=["./instructions"]), ), ) Relative paths are resolved against the current directory, not the file that declares them. The text can also be given directly, without files: standing_instructions: source: type: memory soul: Answer in British English. task: Review pull request 12. Its blocks are headed [soul], [agent] and [task]. When such an agent is run with domyn run, its source is used as it is declared: nothing is added to it. attach_instructions(agent, runtime) sets the runtime on an agent that already exists.

standing_instructions: Option Type Default Description source source required Where the instructions come from: local_dir or memory. max_bytes int 32768 Limit on the text of all instructions together, in bytes. See Size limit. local_dir source: Option Type Default Description paths list of paths [] Directories, from which SOUL.md and AGENTS.md (or AGENT.md) are read, and files, read whatever their name. Only the files directly in a directory are read, except .domyn and .agents written as relative paths, which are searched with their subfolders. ~ is expanded. memory source: Option Type Default Description soul str "" Who the agent is. agent str "" What the agent is working on. task str "" A one-off brief.
Skills: instructions the agent loads only when a task needs them. YAML configuration: the rest of an agent's YAML definition. Sessions and commands: the session the default files apply to.

Tools are how an agent acts: it calls them to search, read data, call an API or change something. A tool can be a Python function, an async generator that streams its output, or a tool on a remote MCP server. The model decides when to call a tool from its name, its description and the description of its arguments, so those three matter as much as the code.

Wrap any Python function in a FunctionTool: from domyn.agents import FunctionTool async def search_documents(query: str, max_results: int = 5) -> str: """Search the document store for relevant content. Args: query: The search query in natural language. max_results: Maximum number of results to return. """ results = await perform_search(query, limit=max_results) return format_results(results) tool = FunctionTool(func=search_documents) Then pass it to an agent with Agent(..., tools=[tool]). What the model sees is built from the function: Name: the function's name, search_documents. Description: the first part of the docstring, before the Args: section. Arguments: one per parameter, with the type taken from its annotation. A parameter without a default value is required. Argument descriptions: taken from the Args: section of the docstring, written in the Google style shown above. Once a docstring has an Args: section, it must describe every parameter: a parameter missing from it makes FunctionTool(...) raise a ValidationError. Without an Args: section, each parameter gets a generic description. Instead of the Args: section, you can describe a parameter next to its type with Annotated: from typing import Annotated def get_forecast(city: Annotated[str, "The city name"], days: int = 1) -> str: """Get the weather forecast for a city.""" ... The function can be sync or async. What it returns is what the model reads as the tool's result.

The @tool() decorator turns a function into a FunctionTool and registers it by name, so a YAML configuration can refer to it with reference:: from domyn.agents.core.decorators import tool @tool() async def search_documents(query: str) -> str: """Search documents.""" ... name and description override the defaults: @tool(name="search", description="Search documents"). warning Always write the parentheses. A bare @tool without them does not raise an error, but leaves a function that is not a tool.

Some arguments should come from your configuration, not from the model: an API key, a tenant id, an internal URL. Declare them as ConfigParams: from domyn.agents.tools import ConfigParam async def call_api(query: str, api_key: str) -> str: """Call an external API.""" return await make_request(query, api_key=api_key) tool = FunctionTool( func=call_api, config_params=[ConfigParam(name="api_key", value="sk-...", is_secret=True)], ) A config parameter is left out of the arguments the model sees, so the model never knows it exists. Its value is passed to the function on every call.

A tool can require a person to approve each call before it runs: from domyn.agents import ApprovalType refund_tool = FunctionTool(func=process_refund, approval_type=ApprovalType.USER_CONFIRM) approval_type The person can ApprovalType.USER_CONFIRM Approve or refuse the call ApprovalType.PARAMS_UPDATE Also change the arguments before approving Instead of running the tool, the runner emits a TOOL_NEEDS_FEEDBACK event and waits for the answer. How to answer it, and how approvals can be remembered, is in Tool approvals.

A tool that takes a while can show progress while it works. Write it as an async generator and wrap it in a StreamableFunctionTool: from domyn.agents import Part from domyn.agents.tools.base import UpdateToolResult from domyn.agents.tools import ( StreamableFunctionTool, StreamableToolResult, ) async def analyze_dataset(dataset_id: str): """Analyze a dataset.""" yield StreamableToolResult(data=Part(text="Loading the dataset...\n")) data = await load_data(dataset_id) yield UpdateToolResult(data={"loaded": len(data)}) result = await run_analysis(data) yield f"Analysis complete: {result.summary}" tool = StreamableFunctionTool(func=analyze_dataset) What the generator yields decides where it goes: Yielded value Becomes StreamableToolResult(data=Part(text=...)) Text shown to the user right away, as a partial RESPONSE event. The model reads it too, appended to the tool's result. UpdateToolResult(data={...}) A TOOL_UPDATE event carrying the data, for a progress bar or a status line in your interface. The model does not see it. Any other value The tool's result, the one the model reads. When there are several, only the last one counts. When the agent runs as a sub-agent, or its planner runs with use_stop=True, its text chunks are not shown to the user: they are added to the tool's result instead.
An agent can use the tools of a remote MCP server over streamable HTTP.

Declare the server on the agent, then call initialize_mcp_tools() to fetch its tools: from domyn.agents import Agent from domyn.agents.tools.mcp import MCPServerStreamableHTTPConfig agent = Agent( name="MyAgent", description="Agent with remote tools", instruction="...", llm_provider=llm, mcp_servers=[ MCPServerStreamableHTTPConfig( name="analytics", url="https://analytics.example.com/mcp", ) ], ) await agent.initialize_mcp_tools() After the call, agent.tools holds one tool for each tool of the server, with the name and description the server gives it. Until you call it, the agent has none of them, and nothing tells you so. note An agent loaded from a YAML file with load_application_from_file is already initialized. Call initialize_mcp_tools() only for an agent you build in Python. Set tool_autodiscovery=False to declare a server without fetching its tools.
documents.s: Using every tool of a server

documents.t: To use one tool of a server, create an MCPTool and initialize it: from domyn.agents import MCPTool search_tool = MCPTool( server_url="https://api.example.com/mcp", tool_name="search", ) await search_tool.initialize() agent.tools.append(search_tool) You can also put it in Agent(..., tools=[search_tool]) and let agent.initialize_mcp_tools() initialize it with the others.

For a server that takes a token or an API key, pass it as a header: MCPServerStreamableHTTPConfig( name="analytics", url="https://analytics.example.com/mcp", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer <token>"}, ) MCPTool takes the same headers argument. For a server that requires OAuth, set use_oauth=True. The first time the agent connects, a browser window opens for you to sign in. With use_oauth=True alone, the tokens are kept in memory, so you sign in again each time the process starts. To keep them on disk, under ~/.domyn/mcp_oauth/, use an OAuth provider of type local, as below. MCPServerStreamableHTTPConfig( name="secure_service", url="https://api.example.com/mcp", use_oauth=True, ) By default the agent asks for the read scope and registers itself as "Domyn Agent". To change that, build the OAuth settings yourself and pass them as oauth_provider: from domyn.agents.tools.mcp.oauth_providers import OAuthProviderConfig, build_oauth_provider url = "https://api.example.com/mcp" oauth = OAuthProviderConfig(name="my_oauth", scopes=["read", "write"], client_name="My Agent") MCPServerStreamableHTTPConfig( name="secure_service", url=url, use_oauth=True, oauth_provider=build_oauth_provider(oauth, url), ) An OAuthProviderConfig is of type local unless you set type="in_memory", so the tokens of this example are kept on disk, under ~/.domyn/mcp_oauth/. In YAML, the same settings go in a named oauth_providers: entry. See YAML configuration.

A model can ask for several tools in one answer: read three files, query two servers. The calls that need no approval run at the same time, so the turn waits for the slowest of them rather than for their sum, and their results reach the model together in its next request. A call to a tool that requires approval runs alone and in order: everything the model asked for before it has finished, and nothing after it has started. Those are the calls another may depend on, such as writing a file and then running the tests, and an approval is asked about a call that has not begun. While the approval is pending, the calls after it wait; they run once it is answered, before the model is asked again. See Tool approvals. It is on by default, and an option of the planner strategy, so each agent decides. Turn it off and every call runs after the one before it, in order: from domyn.agents.planner_strategy import ToolUseWithThoughtPlannerStrategy planner = ToolUseWithThoughtPlannerStrategy(parallel_tool_calls=False) or, in YAML: planner_strategies: - name: one_at_a_time type: tool_use_thought parallel_tool_calls: false How many run at the same time at most is the Runner's: Runner(max_parallel_tool_calls=4) (default 8). Tools that run together share the conversation's state, so a tool that changes it should not assume another one is not changing it at the same time.

A hook runs your code around every call of a tool: to check or clean the arguments, to change the result, or to log. Write it with @hook and attach it to the tool with hooks=: from domyn.agents.core.decorators import hook from domyn.agents.hooks import HookPhase @hook(trigger=HookPhase.PRE_TOOL_CALL) def strip_query(tool, tool_args): tool_args["query"] = tool_args["query"].strip() return {"new_tool_args": tool_args} @hook(trigger=HookPhase.POST_TOOL_CALL) def shorten_result(tool, result): result.data = result.data[:2000] return result @hook(trigger=HookPhase.PRE_TOOL_CALL, is_listener=True) def log_call(tool, tool_args): print(f"Calling {tool.name} with query={tool_args['query']!r}") tool = FunctionTool(func=search_documents, hooks=[strip_query, shorten_result, log_call]) Trigger Runs The function receives To change something, return PRE_TOOL_CALL Before the tool runs tool, tool_args {"new_tool_args": tool_args} POST_TOOL_CALL After the tool returns tool, result (a ToolResult, with the return value in result.data) The ToolResult, or {"new_result": result} The function must have parameters with these names: a hook missing one is refused when it is defined. tool_args holds the arguments of the call, together with a few keys the runner adds, such as state and conversation_id. A hook is an updater by default: hooks of this kind run one after the other, each receiving what the previous one returned. With is_listener=True it is a listener: listeners run concurrently, after the updaters, and what they return is ignored. PRE_TOOL_CALL runs after the decision to run the tool has been taken. A hook that must allow or refuse a call uses PRE_TOOL_APPROVAL instead. Every trigger, and hooks on agents, are covered in Hooks.

A Transcriber turns audio into text: a voice note, a recording, a clip from a microphone. It is the piece the voice features are built on, and it can be used on its own: from domyn.agents.audio import LocalTranscriber transcriber = LocalTranscriber() transcript = await transcriber.transcribe("meeting.m4a") print(transcript.text) for segment in transcript.segments: print(f"{segment.start:6.1f}s {segment.text}") There are two, chosen by where the speech model runs: type runs needs local on this machine; no audio leaves it the audio extra openai on a server speaking OpenAI's /v1/audio/transcriptions: OpenAI, vLLM serving a speech model, a gateway the server's URL, and a key if it asks for one

pip install 'domyn[audio]' # or: uv add 'domyn[audio]' The extra installs onnx-asr, which runs speech models with ONNX Runtime on the CPU. It is available on Python 3.11 to 3.14: ONNX Runtime has no release for 3.15 yet. The default model is NVIDIA's Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3: 25 European languages, Italian and English among them, recognized without being told which, with punctuation. Before it, Silero finds the pauses in the audio (voice activity detection): that is what lets an hour-long recording through, and what gives each segment its start and end. Nothing is downloaded until it is needed. Installing the extra downloads no model, and creating a LocalTranscriber loads nothing. The first transcription downloads the model, about 670 MB, into ~/.domyn/models/, once; later ones read it from there. To download it ahead, for example before working offline, call prepare(), which also tells you when there is something to download: await transcriber.prepare(on_download=print) # Downloading the speech model nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 (about 670 MB) to /Users/you/.domyn/models: only this once. A download goes into a temporary directory that is renamed into place when complete, so an interrupted one is started again next time rather than mistaken for a model. The options: field default model nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 any model onnx-asr knows, or a Hugging Face repository, such as onnx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo quantization int8 None for full precision: about 2.5 GB for the default model, for little difference in practice vad true false transcribes the audio in one piece, without segments: only for short clips language detected an ISO 639-1 code such as it. Parakeet detects the language itself and ignores it; Whisper and Canary models use it models_dir ~/.domyn/models where models are downloaded WAV files are read as they are. Any other format (mp3, m4a, Ogg/Opus voice notes, webm…) is converted first with ffmpeg, which has to be installed (brew install ffmpeg, apt install ffmpeg); without it, those formats fail with an error that says so.

from domyn.agents.audio import OpenAICompatibleTranscriber transcriber = OpenAICompatibleTranscriber( url="http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions", model="openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo", ) The audio is sent as it is, in any format the server accepts, so no ffmpeg is needed. The fields: field default url https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions the full transcriptions URL model whisper-1 the model name the server expects api_key none sent as a Bearer token api_key_env none an environment variable holding the key, read when a request is sent. With neither, no key is sent: a vLLM started without --api-key language detected sent to the server when set response_format verbose_json also returns the language, the duration and the segments; json for a server or model that only returns the text timeout 300 seconds

transcribe() takes a path or the audio's bytes (with filename=, whose extension says the format) and returns a Transcript: field text the whole text segments start, end (seconds) and text of each stretch of speech; empty when the engine gives none language the language set, or the one the server detected duration the length of the audio, in seconds, when known Audio that cannot be transcribed raises TranscriptionError, with a message saying what to do: install the extra or ffmpeg, check the file, check the server. The audio and what was said in it are logged only at debug level.

A transcriber is declared by its type, with the fields above: from domyn.agents.audio import resolve_transcriber transcriber = resolve_transcriber({"type": "openai", "url": "...", "api_key_env": "ASR_KEY"}) A transcriber of your own is a subclass of Transcriber with its own type and a transcribe method; it is found by that type like the built-in ones.

The Telegram, Slack and WhatsApp channels take a transcriber (an instance or its configuration). A voice note or audio file a user sends is downloaded, transcribed, and given to the agent as text right after the audio, marked as a transcription: [Voice message, transcribed] …. The audio stays attached. When there is no transcriber, or the audio cannot be transcribed, the text says so instead, so the agent can tell the user rather than answer as if nothing had been said. from domyn.agents.channels import TelegramChannel channel = TelegramChannel(token=token, transcriber={"type": "local"}) With the local transcriber, the first voice note downloads the model, so that one answer takes longer.
onnx-asr is MIT. The Parakeet model is released by NVIDIA under CC-BY-4.0, which allows commercial use with attribution; Silero VAD is MIT.

The domyn command is installed with the package (see Installation). Every command accepts -h / --help. Command What it does domyn run Chat with an agent in the terminal domyn setup Choose the provider, model and agent of domyn run domyn init Create a new project with an example agent domyn skills List the skills the configuration loads domyn skill Show a skill, or stop loading it domyn export Save the configuration, with its skills and instructions, into a new folder to share domyn connect Connect an agent to the Domyn platform as a relay worker The commands available inside a domyn run session, such as /model or /resume, are listed in Sessions and commands.

Given before the command: domyn --log-level DEBUG run. Option Type Default Description --log-level str WARNING for run, setup, init, skills and skill; INFO for the servers Logging level: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL. Any other value is taken as INFO. --version Prints the version and exits.

Before running any command, domyn reads a .env file from the current directory or the nearest parent directory that has one, then ~/.domyn/credentials, where the setup wizard saves API keys. A variable already set in the environment is never replaced, and .env comes before the credentials file. These variables are what ${VAR} in a YAML configuration refers to. With --project, the project's own credentials file is read first, and ~/.domyn/credentials supplies only the keys the project does not set. run, setup, skills, skill and export take --project <name> to work on a project, a separate configuration, instead of the default one in ~/.domyn. A name means ~/.domyn/projects/<name>; a value containing / or starting with . or ~ is the path of a project folder.

domyn run [FILE] [MESSAGE] [OPTIONS] Opens a chat session with an agent. See Sessions and commands for the session itself. Argument Description FILE A .py or .yaml file defining the agent. Without it, the agent configured in ~/.domyn/config.yaml; the first time, the setup wizard runs before the session. MESSAGE Sent as the first message of the session. From a Python file, the agent is the one that is not a sub-agent of another; from a YAML file, its entrypoint. Option Type Default Description --agent-name, -a str The variable holding the agent, when a Python file defines more than one. --resume flag off Continues a past conversation: --resume <conversation_id>, or --resume alone to choose one from a list. The id takes the place of MESSAGE, so the two cannot be combined. For a conversation started from a file, give the same FILE. --expand-skills flag off Gives the model every skill in full up front, instead of an index it reads from on demand. Uses more of the context window. --skill-sections flag off Lists each skill's sections in the index. Uses more of the context window. --verbose, -v flag off Shows internal events: model calls, hooks, hand-offs. --no-banner flag off Skips the startup banner. --project str Runs a project instead of the default configuration. The banner shows its name. --voice flag off Starts with push-to-talk on, as /voice does: hold the space bar to speak. Needs the audio extra. See Talking instead of typing. The skills and the standing instructions are those the configuration declares; no option adds or removes any. When the session ends, it prints the conversation id and the command that resumes it, with FILE when the session was started from one: domyn run agent.yaml --resume <conversation_id>.

domyn setup [--show] [--project NAME] [--import FOLDER] Runs the setup wizard: provider, model and API key, standing instructions, built-in tools and skills, saved to ~/.domyn/config.yaml and, for the key, ~/.domyn/credentials. Run again over an existing configuration, it shows each part and asks whether to keep it. See the CLI quickstart and Configuring the CLI. Option Description --show Prints the active configuration and exits. --project Sets up a project instead of the default configuration, creating it if it does not exist. --import Creates a new project from a folder made by domyn export, named after the folder unless --project gives a name. The wizard shows each exported setting and asks whether to keep it; when you do not keep the skills, it also offers the built-in skills the export does not include, unticked. It warns when the export was made by another version of domyn-agents, or does not say which. Cannot be combined with --show.

domyn init [PROJECT_NAME] [--directory DIR] [--force] Creates a new project with uv: a pyproject.toml that depends on domyn[cli], an example agent.py with two tools, a README.md and a Dockerfile that runs domyn serve agent.py, then installs the dependencies with uv sync. uv must be installed. Without PROJECT_NAME, it asks for one. Option Type Default Description --directory, -d str ./PROJECT_NAME Where to create the project. --force, -f flag off Deletes the directory first if it exists and is not empty. Without it, init stops. Then set the provider in agent.py and run uv run domyn run agent.py.

domyn skills Lists the skills the configuration loads, ./.domyn/config.yaml when the current directory has one and ~/.domyn/config.yaml otherwise: their names, descriptions, sections and files, and why any is unavailable. A relative path in the configuration is read from the current directory, as domyn run reads it. Option Type Description --project str Uses a project's configuration.

domyn skill show|remove NAME Works on the skills the global ~/.domyn/config.yaml loads, whatever the current directory, or a project's with --project. Action Description show Prints the skill: its file, its sections and its text. NAME#SECTION prints one ## section. remove Removes the entry that names the skill, its folder or its .md file, from the configuration. No file is deleted. A skill loaded through a listed folder, such as ./.domyn/skills, has no entry of its own: nothing is removed, and the command says how to stop loading it. Option Description --project Uses a project's configuration.

domyn export FOLDER [--config FILE] [--project NAME] Saves the configuration into the new folder FOLDER, with the skills and standing instructions it uses, so it can be shared or run elsewhere. The folder is a project: run it where it is with domyn run --project FOLDER, move it to ~/.domyn/projects/<name> and run domyn run --project <name>, or create a new project from it with domyn setup --import FOLDER. Option Type Default Description --config path the one domyn run uses The configuration file to export. --project str Exports a project instead of the default configuration. A skill is copied as its SKILL.md plus the files its external_files lists; anything else in its folder is left out and named in the report. API keys, approvals and conversation history are never copied: a key written in the configuration is replaced by a ${VAR} reference, and the report names the variables to set. FOLDER must not exist, or be empty. The folder also gets a hidden .info file with the version of domyn-agents, the date, the Python version and the platform, which domyn setup --import checks. /export FOLDER does the same from inside a session.

domyn connect MODULE:SYMBOL --channel-id ID --base-url HOST Serves an agent or a LangGraph graph on a relay channel, for a DelegateAgent in another application to call. domyn expose is an older name for the same command, still accepted. It needs the platform SDK, which provides the relay's address and headers. See Remote agents for the argument, the relay, and LangGraph graphs. Option Environment variable Type Default Description --channel-id DOMYN_CHANNEL_ID str Channel to serve. --space-id DOMYN_SPACE_ID str Space the channel belongs to. --configuration-id DOMYN_CONFIGURATION_ID str Configuration of the space to use. Optional. --base-url DOMYN_BASE_URL str Relay host, with an optional port. The relay is reached at wss://<host>/relay/v1/ws, or ws:// for localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1. --target str Serves several channels from one process. Repeatable; each is channel_id=…,space_id=…,base_url=…,configuration_id=…, where only channel_id is required. space_id and base_url default to --space-id and --base-url; configuration_id defaults to --configuration-id only when the target sets no space_id. --max-concurrency int 8 Turns run at the same time. Beyond that, as many more wait, and further requests are refused. --platform-tools / --no-platform-tools flag on when the SDK is installed, else off Adds to the entrypoint agent every tool the platform offers that it does not already declare. --platform-tools without the SDK stops and names the version it needs. --tool-refresh-interval float 0 With --platform-tools, looks for new platform tools every this many seconds. 0 never does. DOMYN_API_KEY must be set; it is sent to the relay in the api-key header.

Every event is a BaseEvent (domyn.agents.core) whose event_type is an ExecutionEventType. This page uses the values, such as tool_start; in Python, compare with the enum member, such as ExecutionEventType.TOOL_START. How to consume them is in Events and streaming.

Field Type Description event_type ExecutionEventType What happened. author str The agent the event belongs to; user for inputs. content list[Part] Text and other parts. See Parts. action action The call the event is about, for tool and agent events. See Actions. is_partial bool More pieces of the same output follow. error_code str | None On errors: a short code, such as the exception type. error_message str | None On errors: the description. metadata dict Type-specific data, listed per type below. need_feedback bool The event is a question to the user, and the turn ends with it. event_id str Unique id of the event. conversation_id str The conversation. turn_id, interaction_id str Identify the turn the event belongs to. A turn resumed after an approval keeps both. timestamp datetime When the event was created.

Field Description text Text for the user. thought The agent's reasoning, or a status line, not meant as the answer. code, html, chart, rich_text, link, file, metadata, guardrail_result Structured parts, for interfaces that render them.

Class On Fields AgentAction agent_start, agent_call, a remote agent's agent_end name (the agent), parameters (the task, or the agent's own invocation parameters), thought ToolAction tool_start, tool_update, tool_end, tool_error, a local team member's agent_end name, parameters, thought, call_id, observation (the result, on tool_end and tool_error) FeedbackAction tool_needs_feedback, tool_feedback as ToolAction, plus approval_type, approve, remember_scope, remember_pattern; parameters is a list of name–value pairs that can be edited AuthenticationAction tool_needs_feedback as ToolAction, for an MCP tool whose OAuth credentials must be renewed before it runs Every action also has an optional message.

Type When Carries agent_start An agent starts its part of the turn: the root agent first, then each team member it hands off to. action: AgentAction with the task; content: the task as text. agent_call An agent hands off to a team member. Followed by that member's agent_start. action: AgentAction naming the member, with its arguments and the reason in thought. agent_end An agent finishes. For the root agent, the last event of the turn. For a team member, its answer in content and its final call in action. Empty for the root agent.

Type When Carries llm_start Before each model call. metadata["context_usage"]: message_tokens and tool_definition_tokens (estimated), correction_tokens (the provider's count of the last request minus the estimate of it, 0 without a count), context_window, threshold_tokens and strategy, each None when it does not apply. threshold_tokens is set only when a compaction can happen; content: a status line. llm_end After each model call. content: a status line and, for a tool_use_thought agent, the model's reasoning as a thought part. response The reply, when it is not streamed; text a streaming tool shows right away (is_partial); a reply forwarded unchanged with FORWARD_VERBATIM (metadata["forward_verbatim"]); the message of a hook that stops the turn; a question to the user (need_feedback). content: the text. response_token A piece of a streamed reply, for an agent with stream=True. content: the next piece; is_partial is True. external_part Content pushed into a running turn with Runner.push_parts, from outside the agent. content; the model sees it only when its metadata marks it visible. llm_provider_error The model's API failed, with the react planner only. error_message.

Type When Carries tool_start The model called a tool. action: ToolAction with the arguments and the thought. tool_update A streaming tool reported progress with UpdateToolResult. Not shown to the model. content[0].metadata: the data the tool yielded. tool_end The tool returned. Also when a call was refused at the approval gate: the refusal is the result. action.observation: the result. tool_error The tool raised. error_code: the exception type; error_message and action.observation: its message. tool_needs_feedback The tool needs approval before it runs. The turn ends with it. action: FeedbackAction for the pending call; metadata: approval_subject, approval_scopes, approval_pattern, approval_parts.

Type When Carries hook_start Before a hook runs. metadata["hook_name"]. hook_update A hook emitted content without finishing. content, metadata["hook_name"]. hook_end A hook finished. content it emitted, metadata["hook_name"]. hook_error A hook raised. error_code: the exception type; error_message; metadata["hook_name"].

Type When Carries context_compaction_start The conversation is about to be shortened: the request reached the threshold, the provider rejected it as too long, or a compaction was requested. metadata: tokens_before, threshold_tokens and rejected (the provider rejected the request), or requested: True. context_compacted The compaction finished. metadata: changed (something was removed or summarized). At the threshold, also tokens_before, tokens_after, threshold_tokens and sufficient (the result fits under the threshold); on request, requested: True, events_dropped and tokens_saved. error_occurred The agent could not continue. The last event of the turn. error_message; content: a description, from a planner; error_code, from the runner, such as RequiredSkillUnavailable.

These are passed to Runner.run() as user_input. Type Purpose user_input A message from the user: content with its text. tool_feedback The answer to a tool_needs_feedback: its action, with approve set and, optionally, edited parameters and a remember_scope. See Tool approvals. compaction_requested Asks for a compaction now, instead of waiting for the threshold. The stream is only context_compaction_start and context_compacted (only the latter, with changed: False, for a planner that cannot compact), and the request is not added to the conversation. See Context compaction.

Every key of a YAML application file. How to write and run one is in YAML configuration. Any string value can contain ${NAME}, replaced with the environment variable NAME when the file is loaded; an unset variable stops the load with an error. Relative paths (path, workspace) are resolved against the current directory.

Key Type Default Description version "1.0" "1.0" Format version. Must be the string "1.0": unquoted, 1.0 is a number, and the load fails with Unsupported configuration version. entrypoint str the last agent, in dependency order Name of the agent the user talks to. llm_providers list [] See llm_providers. planner_strategies list [] See planner_strategies. context_managers list [] Context managers referenced by name from planner_strategies. Each needs name and type, and the react ones more keys. See Planner strategies. tools list [] See tools. tool_bundles list [] See tool_bundles. mcp_servers list [] See mcp_servers. oauth_providers list [] See oauth_providers. hooks list [] See hooks. agents list required See agents. metadata mapping none Free-form keys for the application that reads the file. The loader keeps them and does nothing with them; the interactive CLI's /config shows their names only. final bool false Kept with the configuration as a marker for the application. Nothing in the framework enforces it.

Key Type Default Description name str the model_name Name agents refer to. type domyn | openai | anthropic | vllm | cerebras | open_router | custom required, unless reference The provider. model_name str required The model. reference str Instead of type: the name of a provider registered in Python with @llm_provider, copied under this entry's name. config_params dict With reference: options to change on the copy; dictionaries are merged. With type: options added to the entry's own. Any option except type, model_name, name, url and reference. The other keys depend on type (url, api_key, generation_params, context_window, …). See LLM providers.

Key Type Default Description name str the type Name agents refer to. type tool_use_thought | tool_use | react required The strategy. context_manager str per type Name of an entry of context_managers. The other options (max_iterations, compactor, …) are listed in Planner strategies.

Key Type Default Description name str required Name of the function in path, which is also the name the model sees. type function | StreamableFunctionTool required StreamableFunctionTool for an async generator. See Tools. path str required The Python file that defines the function. approval_type user_confirm | params_update none Each call waits for approval. See Tool approvals. hooks list of str [] Names of pre_tool_approval, pre_tool_call and post_tool_call hooks. The description the model reads is the function's docstring.

Key Type Default Description name str required The tool's name on the server. type mcp required server_url str required The server's streamable HTTP endpoint. headers dict[str, str] none HTTP headers sent to the server, for example Authorization. use_oauth bool false Sign in with OAuth. oauth_provider str the in-memory default Name of an entry of oauth_providers. approval_type user_confirm | params_update none Each call waits for approval. hooks list of str [] Names of pre_tool_approval, pre_tool_call and post_tool_call hooks.

Key Type Default Description name str required Name agents refer to. reference str required A tool registered in Python with @tool(). hooks list of str [] Hooks to attach. Two more types exist: rest, an HTTP endpoint called as a tool, and delegate, a tool declared here and run by the application, used with remote agents. An entry whose type is unknown, or that cannot be built from its keys, is skipped with a warning in the log naming the tool and its type, and the agents that list it are loaded without it.

Key Type Default Description name str required Name agents refer to in tool_bundles. bundles list of files | shell [files, shell] Which tools: files (read_file, list_dir, glob_files, grep, write_file, append_file, edit_file), shell (run_command, check_command, list_commands, stop_command). workspace str the current directory The directory the tools can reach. sandbox local local Where commands run. isolate_environment bool true Commands see only a fixed set of environment variables (PATH, HOME, …), plus allowed_env. allowed_env list of str [] Further environment variables commands may see.

Key Type Default Description name str required Name agents refer to in mcp_servers. url str required The server's streamable HTTP endpoint. tool_autodiscovery bool true Fetch the server's tools when the agent is initialized. headers dict[str, str] none HTTP headers sent to the server. use_oauth bool false Sign in with OAuth. oauth_provider str the in-memory default Name of an entry of oauth_providers. timeout float 30.0 Seconds to wait for the server.

Key Type Default Description name str required Name servers and tools refer to. __default__ is reserved. type local | in_memory local local keeps the tokens on disk, in_memory only for the life of the process. storage_dir str ~/.domyn/mcp_oauth Where local keeps the tokens. scopes list of str [read] Scopes to request. client_name str Domyn Agent Name the client registers with. client_id str none A client registered in advance with the server. Without it, the client registers itself. client_secret str none Secret of client_id, when the server requires one. callback_port int 45678 Local port of the sign-in callback, http://localhost:<port>/callback. A server or tool with use_oauth and no oauth_provider uses an in-memory provider with the defaults above.

Key Type Default Description name str required Name of the function in path, and the name agents and tools refer to. type listener | updater required, unless reference listener observes and runs concurrently; updater can change what it receives. trigger pre_agent_call | post_agent_call | on_agent_event | pre_tool_approval | pre_tool_call | post_tool_call required When it runs. The first three attach to agents, the last three to tools. path str required, unless reference or url The Python file that defines the function. url str Instead of path: an HTTP endpoint called as the hook. method GET | POST | PUT | DELETE | PATCH POST With url: the HTTP method. headers dict[str, str] none With url: HTTP headers sent with each call. timeout float 300.0 With url: seconds to wait for the endpoint. reference str Instead of path and type: a hook registered in Python with @hook. break_on_error bool true Whether the hook raising stops the turn. silent bool false Keep the events the hook produces out of the conversation history. They are still emitted. on_event_triggers list of event types see Hooks For on_agent_event: the event types it runs on, such as tool_end. See Hooks.

Key Type Default Description name str required 1 to 30 characters. description str required What the agent does, at most 1,000 characters. In a team, the main agent chooses a member from it. instruction str required The system instruction. llm_provider str required Name of an entry of llm_providers, or of a provider registered in Python. planner_strategy str tool_use_thought with its defaults Name of an entry of planner_strategies, or of a strategy registered in Python. max_iterations int the strategy's Kept on the agent, but not read by any strategy: the limit on a turn is the max_iterations of its planner_strategy. memory_manager mapping none Long-term memory: type (filesystem or remote), execution_mode (automatic or agentic) and the manager's options. See Conversations and memory. stream bool false Stream the reply. See Events and streaming. tools list of str [] Names of entries of tools, or of tools registered in Python. tool_bundles list of str [] Names of entries of tool_bundles. mcp_servers list of str [] Names of entries of mcp_servers. sub_agents list of str [] The agents of its team. See Orchestration. context_visibility standard | peers | global standard What history the agent sees. See Orchestration. handoff_scope explicit | direct_peers | global explicit Which agents it may hand off to. See Orchestration. hooks list of str [] Names of pre_agent_call, post_agent_call and on_agent_event hooks. skills mapping none source: {type: local_dir, paths: [...]}. See Skills. standing_instructions mapping none source: {type: local_dir, paths: [...]}. See Standing instructions. type agent | delegate agent delegate for an agent that runs in another process. See Remote agents. Keys that are not recognized are ignored without an error.
